results.content:
1	# Settings Files
2	
3	**Optionally** you can store settings in files, dynaconf supports multiple
4	file formats, you are recommended to choose one format but you can also use
5	mixed settings formats across your application.
6	
7	
8	!!! tip
9	    You are not required to use settings files, if not specified dynaconf
10	    can load your data only from [environment variables](envvars.md)
11	
12	## Supported formats
13	
14	- **.toml** - Default and **recommended** file format.
15	- **.yaml|.yml** - Recommended for Django applications (see [YAML Caveats](#yaml-caveats)).
16	- **.json** - Useful to reuse existing or exported settings.
17	- **.ini** - Useful to reuse legacy settings.
18	- **.py** - **Not Recommended** but supported for backwards compatibility.
19	- **.env** - Useful to automate the loading of environment variables.
20	
21	!!! info
22	    Create your settings in the desired format and specify it on `settings_files`
23	    argument on your dynaconf instance or pass it in `-f <format>` if using `dynaconf init` command.
24	
25	!!! tip
26	    Can't find the file format you need for your settings?
27	    You can create your custom loader and read any data source.
28	    read more on [extending dynaconf](advanced.md)
29	
30	!!! warning
31	    To use the `.ini` or `.properties` file format you need to install an extra dependency
32	    `pip install configobj` or `pip install dynaconf[ini]`
33	
34	## Reading settings from files
35	
36	On files by default dynaconf loads all the existing keys and sections
37	as first level settings.
38	
39	=== "settings.toml"
40	    ```toml
41	    name = "Bruno"
42	    ```
43	
44	=== "settings.yaml"
45	    ```yaml
46	    name: Bruno
47	    ```
48	
49	=== "settings.json"
50	    ```json
51	    {"name": "Bruno"}
52	    ```
53	
54	=== "settings.ini"
55	    ```ini
56	    name = 'Bruno'
57	    ```
58	
59	=== "settings.py"
60	    ```py
61	    NAME = "Bruno"
62	    ```
63	    > ⚠️ on `.py` files dynaconf only read UPPERCASE variables.
64	
65	Then on your application code:
66	
67	```python
68	settings.name == "Bruno"
69	```
70	
71	!!! info
72	    The default encoding when loading the settings files is `utf-8` and it can be customized
73	    via `encoding` parameter.
74	
75	## Loading setting files
76	
77	Dynaconf will start looking for each file defined in `settings_files` from the folder where your entry point python file is located (like `app.py`). Then, it will look at each parent down to the root of the system. For each visited folder, it will also try looking inside a `/config` folder.
78	
79	- If you define [root_path](configuration.md/#root_path), it will look start looking from there, instead. Keep in mind that `root_path` is relative to `cwd`, which is from where the python interpreter was called.
80	- Absolute paths are recognized and dynaconf will attempt to load them directly.
81	- For each file specified in `settings_files` dynaconf will also try to load an optional `name`**.local.**`extension`. Eg, `settings_file="settings.toml"` will look for `settings.local.toml` too.
82	- Globs are accepted.
83	
84	Define it in your settings instance or export the corresponding envvars.
85	
86	```python
87	# default
88	settings = Dynaconf(settings_files=["settings.toml", "*.yaml"])
89	
90	# using root_path
91	settings = Dynaconf(
92	    root_path="my/project/root",
93	    settings_files=["settings.toml", "*.yaml"]
94	)
95	```
96	
97	```bash
98	export ROOT_PATH_FOR_DYNACONF='my/project/root'
99	export SETTINGS_FILES_FOR_DYNACONF='["settings.toml", "*.yaml"]'
100	```
101	
102	!!! info
103	    To use `python -m module`, where the module uses dynaconf you will need to
104	    specify your `settings.toml` path, for example, like this: `settings_file="module/config/settings.toml"`.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## Includes and Preloads
109	
110	If you need, you can specify files to be loaded before or after the `settings_files` using the options [preload](configuration.md#preload) and [includes](configuration.md#includes). Their loading strategy is more strict, and will use `root_path` as the basepath for the relative paths provided. If `root_path` is not defined, `includes` will also try using the last found settings directory as the basepath.
111	
112	They can be defined in the Dynaconf instance or in a file:
113	
114	```py
115	# in Dynaconf instance
116	settings = Dynaconf(
117	    includes=["path/to/file.toml", "or/a/glob/*.yaml"],
118	    preload=["path/to/file.toml", "or/a/glob/*.yaml"])
119	```
120	
121	or
122	
123	```toml
124	# in toml file
125	dynaconf_include = ["path/to/file.toml"]
126	key = value
127	anotherkey = value
128	```
129	
130	---
131	
132	## Layered environments on files
133	
134	It is also possible to make dynaconf read the files separated by layered
135	environments so each section or first level key is loaded as a
136	distinct environment.
137	
138	### Bypassing environment processing
139	
140	If you want to load a file without any environment-based filtering or layers,
141	you can use `env=False` when calling `load_file()`. This will load all top-level
142	variables from the file directly, regardless of whether environment support is
143	enabled in your configuration.
144	
145	```python
146	settings.load_file(path="config.toml", env=False)
147	```
148	
149	This is available starting from version 3.2.11. The file will be treated as
150	environment-agnostic, with all top-level keys loaded at the global level.
151	
152	**Note:** When using `env=False`, the file is processed using the environment-less
153	loading path, which means section headers like `[development]` or `[production]`
154	will be treated as regular keys rather than environment sections.
155	
156	=== "config.py"
157	    ```py
158	    settings = Dynaconf(environments=True)
159	    ```
160	
161	=== "settings.toml"
162	    ```toml
163	    [default]
164	    name = ""
165	    [development]
166	    name = "developer"
167	    [production]
168	    name = "admin"
169	    ```
170	
171	=== "settings.yaml"
172	    ```yaml
173	    default:
174	        name: ''
175	    development:
176	        name: developer
177	    production:
178	        name: admin
179	    ```
180	
181	=== "settings.json"
182	    ```json
183	    {
184	        "default": {
185	            "name": ""
186	        },
187	        "development": {
188	            "name": "developer"
189	        },
190	        "production": {
191	            "name": "admin"
192	        }
193	    }
194	    ```
195	
196	=== "settings.ini"
197	    ```ini
198	    [default]
199	    name = ""
200	    [development]
201	    name = "developer"
202	    [production]
203	    name = "admin"
204	    ```
205	
206	!!! info

# Settings Files

**Optionally** you can store settings in files, dynaconf supports multiple
file formats, you are recommended to choose one format but you can also use
mixed settings formats across your application.


!!! tip
    You are not required to use settings files, if not specified dynaconf
    can load your data only from [environment variables](envvars.md)

## Supported formats

- **.toml** - Default and **recommended** file format.
- **.yaml|.yml** - Recommended for Django applications (see [YAML Caveats](#yaml-caveats)).
- **.json** - Useful to reuse existing or exported settings.
- **.ini** - Useful to reuse legacy settings.
- **.py** - **Not Recommended** but supported for backwards compatibility.
- **.env** - Useful to automate the loading of environment variables.

!!! info
    Create your settings in the desired format and specify it on `settings_files`
    argument on your dynaconf instance or pass it in `-f <format>` if using `dynaconf init` command.

!!! tip
    Can't find the file format you need for your settings?
    You can create your custom loader and read any data source.
    read more on [extending dynaconf](advanced.md)

!!! warning
    To use the `.ini` or `.properties` file format you need to install an extra dependency
    `pip install configobj` or `pip install dynaconf[ini]`

## Reading settings from files

On files by default dynaconf loads all the existing keys and sections
as first level settings.

=== "settings.toml"
    ```toml
    name = "Bruno"
    ```

=== "settings.yaml"
    ```yaml
    name: Bruno
    ```

=== "settings.json"
    ```json
    {"name": "Bruno"}
    ```

=== "settings.ini"
    ```ini
    name = 'Bruno'
    ```

=== "settings.py"
    ```py
    NAME = "Bruno"
    ```
    > ⚠️ on `.py` files dynaconf only read UPPERCASE variables.

Then on your application code:

```python
settings.name == "Bruno"
```

!!! info
    The default encoding when loading the settings files is `utf-8` and it can be customized
    via `encoding` parameter.

## Loading setting files

Dynaconf will start looking for each file defined in `settings_files` from the folder where your entry point python file is located (like `app.py`). Then, it will look at each parent down to the root of the system. For each visited folder, it will also try looking inside a `/config` folder.

- If you define [root_path](configuration.md/#root_path), it will look start looking from there, instead. Keep in mind that `root_path` is relative to `cwd`, which is from where the python interpreter was called.
- Absolute paths are recognized and dynaconf will attempt to load them directly.
- For each file specified in `settings_files` dynaconf will also try to load an optional `name`**.local.**`extension`. Eg, `settings_file="settings.toml"` will look for `settings.local.toml` too.
- Globs are accepted.

Define it in your settings instance or export the corresponding envvars.

```python
# default
settings = Dynaconf(settings_files=["settings.toml", "*.yaml"])

# using root_path
settings = Dynaconf(
    root_path="my/project/root",
    settings_files=["settings.toml", "*.yaml"]
)
```

```bash
export ROOT_PATH_FOR_DYNACONF='my/project/root'
export SETTINGS_FILES_FOR_DYNACONF='["settings.toml", "*.yaml"]'
```

!!! info
    To use `python -m module`, where the module uses dynaconf you will need to
    specify your `settings.toml` path, for example, like this: `settings_file="module/config/settings.toml"`.

---

## Includes and Preloads

If you need, you can specify files to be loaded before or after the `settings_files` using the options [preload](configuration.md#preload) and [includes](configuration.md#includes). Their loading strategy is more strict, and will use `root_path` as the basepath for the relative paths provided. If `root_path` is not defined, `includes` will also try using the last found settings directory as the basepath.

They can be defined in the Dynaconf instance or in a file:

```py
# in Dynaconf instance
settings = Dynaconf(
    includes=["path/to/file.toml", "or/a/glob/*.yaml"],
    preload=["path/to/file.toml", "or/a/glob/*.yaml"])
```

or

```toml
# in toml file
dynaconf_include = ["path/to/file.toml"]
key = value
anotherkey = value
```

---

## Layered environments on files

It is also possible to make dynaconf read the files separated by layered
environments so each section or first level key is loaded as a
distinct environment.

### Bypassing environment processing

If you want to load a file without any environment-based filtering or layers,
you can use `env=False` when calling `load_file()`. This will load all top-level
variables from the file directly, regardless of whether environment support is
enabled in your configuration.

```python
settings.load_file(path="config.toml", env=False)
```

This is available starting from version 3.2.11. The file will be treated as
environment-agnostic, with all top-level keys loaded at the global level.

**Note:** When using `env=False`, the file is processed using the environment-less
loading path, which means section headers like `[development]` or `[production]`
will be treated as regular keys rather than environment sections.

=== "config.py"
    ```py
    settings = Dynaconf(environments=True)
    ```

=== "settings.toml"
    ```toml
    [default]
    name = ""
    [development]
    name = "developer"
    [production]
    name = "admin"
    ```

=== "settings.yaml"
    ```yaml
    default:
        name: ''
    development:
        name: developer
    production:
        name: admin
    ```

=== "settings.json"
    ```json
    {
        "default": {
            "name": ""
        },
        "development": {
            "name": "developer"
        },
        "production": {
            "name": "admin"
        }
    }
    ```

=== "settings.ini"
    ```ini
    [default]
    name = ""
    [development]
    name = "developer"
    [production]
    name = "admin"
    ```

!!! info
    You can define a custom environment using the name you want, like `[testing]` or `[anything]`

    `[default]` and `[global]` are the only environments that are special.

=== "program.py"

    Then in your program, you can use environment variables
    to switch environments.

    `#!bash export ENV_FOR_DYNACONF=development`

    ```python
    settings.name == "developer"
    ```

    `#!bash export ENV_FOR_DYNACONF=production`

    ```python
    settings.name == "admin"
    ```

!!! warning
    On **Flask** and **Django** extensions the default behaviour is already
    the layered environments.
    Also to switch the environment you use `#!bash export FLASK_ENV=production` or `#!bash export DJANGO_ENV=production` respectively.

!!! tip
    It is also possible to switch environments programmatically passing
    `env="development"` to `Dynaconf` class on instantiation.

### YAML Caveats

#### Nonetypes

Yaml parser used by dynaconf (ruamel.yaml) reads undefined values as `None` so

```yaml
key:
key: ~
key: null
```

All those 3 keys will be parsed as python's `None` object.

When using a validator to set a default value for those values you might want to use one of:

```py
Validator("key", default="thing", apply_default_on_none=True)
```

This way dynaconf will consider the default value even if the setting is `None` on yaml.

or on yaml you can set the value to `@empty`

```yaml
key: "@empty"
```
>> **NEW** in 3.1.9

steps.message:
## Summary

I've implemented the `env=False` feature to bypass environment-based layer system when loading configuration files in Dynaconf. Here's what was changed:

### Changes Made

1. **`dynaconf/base.py`** - Modified `load_file()` method:
   - Added documentation for the new `env=False` option
   - When `env=False` is passed, it's internally mapped to a special marker value `"_envless"`

2. **`dynaconf/loaders/base.py`** - Modified `BaseLoader` class:
   - Updated `load()` method to detect the `"_envless"` marker and bypass environment processing
   - Enhanced `_envless_load()` method to flatten environment sections when present in files
   - Added fallback to ensure data is loaded even when key parameter doesn't match any data key

3. **`docs/settings_files.md`** - Added documentation section:
   - Explains how to use `env=False` to bypass environment processing
   - Documents the behavior with files containing environment sections
   - Marks the feature as available from version 3.2.11

### Usage

```python
from dynaconf import Dynaconf

settings = Dynaconf(environments=True)

# Load a file without environment filtering
settings.load_file(path="config.toml", env=False)

# All top-level variables are loaded directly, regardless of sections
settings.MY_KEY  # Available at top level
```

### Behavior

- **Flat files**: All keys are loaded at the top level
- **Files with sections**: Section contents are flattened, with later sections overwriting earlier ones
- **Mixed content**: Both top-level keys and section contents are loaded at the top level

This feature integrates seamlessly with existing validation, source metadata tracking, and all other Dynaconf behaviors while only changing how environment processing is handled for that specific file load operation.
